new: To revise: call engine_manual_apply (ASK 421) in the same batch as SET LOCAL truth.session_id. First preview, with p_write false: it refuses unless the base is the max version and has the given md5, and unless each pair's old text occurs exactly once when that pair is applied; it returns the new md5, length and per-pair counts. Then write with p_write true and that md5 and length: it inserts version+1 with its summary, and its `engine_manual_log` row dated by the Central date. Readers preview the same pairs and compare the md5; after the write, the readback is mrb.cjs (ASK 420(b)). EXECUTE is revoked from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated. Limit: an old text that overlaps itself is counted once.

new:
- A LINK LABEL "LINK D<n>" OR "LINK C<n>" IS KEPT AS "LINK <n>" (ASK 423; C2B Extract, D3B Extract, C3B Extract, Build Save Body, Assume Check Build; engine only):
    - Why: in run 39266 the Oracle's round 2 list and the defender's round 3 answers labelled links "LINK D5" and "LINK D5 [premise 1]". Assume Check Build looks for "LINK <n>" blocks, so every premise found no block ("(no LINK 1 block found in [CR3])"), and E-PREM read 0 blocks in the defender's round 3.
    - What it does, the rounds: one block, identical in the three nodes, runs the node's own code and then rewrites its output. A label "LINK D<n>" or "LINK C<n>" at a line head (after an optional heading mark, list number or bold) becomes "LINK <n>"; the rest of the line and every other line are untouched. Only the side whose chain the round answers or attacks is rewritten, and only n inside that chain: C2B and D3B take side D, bounded by the defender's declared chain read from D1 Extract (D3B only before its last CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES header); C3B takes side C, bounded by the highest entry number of D3B's list against the challenger. Joint labels, the other side's letter, n outside the bound and markup between LINK and the letter are left as written. The kept raw carries the rewrite; raw_labelled_as_written keeps the model's text in the execution only; round_fix.labels lists each rewrite and each label left alone.
    - The bound reader: chain_count widened to read "D1:" and "1)" heads (run 39266 wrote its chain "D1:" to "D5:", which chain_count reads as 0). Over the 245 stored chains it equals chain_count on all 241 where chain_count is above 0, and reads the other 4 (27665, 38661, 39015, 39266). The library's own readers of the same chain, and the copies of declared() and cecDeclared() in the nodes, are planned under ASK 424.
    - What it does, the record: Build Save Body reads round_fix from the B node when it ran, through a fixed table of node names, and writes "[AUDIT v27: LINK LABELS (<round>, ASK 423) -- REWRITTEN: <entry or block>: <as written> -> <as kept>; ... or none; LEFT AS WRITTEN: ... or none.]" for a round with any label to report. Because it now reads the B node, the v27 heading and placeholder lines of a round that was sent back describe the kept round, not the first reply.
    - What it does, the check: vp4Block takes the premise's own number and first picks the answer header tagged [premise n], else the first header with the link number. When two premises share a link and the answers tag them [premise n], each gets its own block; without the tag both still get the first header with that link number.
    - Live: engine db091b9e (from 3257a833), saved 23:06:39Z on 11-18; library unchanged (sha 7b1cd78b3c25da5c), child unchanged.
    - Shown offline: on 39266, C2B entries 1 to 6 become LINK 5, 5, 4, 4, 3, 1 and D3B "LINK D5 [premise 1]" to "LINK D1" become "LINK 5 [premise 1]" to "LINK 1"; premises 1 to 6 each find their block (none did before); E-PREM blocks in the defender's round 3 go from 0 to 6. Over the 19 stored runs whose rounds hold a line-head LINK with D or C, 7 texts change and 50 do not; with the labels made numeric first, every text is byte-equal after. Plants: "LINK D9" on a 5-link chain, "LINK D1 & D2", "LINK D1-D2", "LINK C2" against the defender, and on the C side "LINK C5" over 3 entries and "LINK D1" are left; "**LINK D3:**" and "### LINK D4 [premise 2]" are rewritten, and on the C side "LINK C2" over 3 entries becomes "LINK 2".
